column1: # Links that are known to be dead and that we cannot fix ourselves.
# Why this file exists: a gate that is red every single run stops being read.
# Two weeks of "yes, still those four" and the fifth — a real, new one — goes
# past unnoticed. So red is reserved for **a dead link nobody has accounted
# for**, and everything in here downgrades to a WARN that still prints on
# It is deliberately NOT a way to make something quiet:
#   * a registered link still prints, every run;
#   * every row carries an owner and a date. On that date it goes back to
#     being red, with no further action from anyone. "We are waiting on X"
#     is only true for so long;
#   * matching is exact-string, never a glob, so a row cannot accidentally
#     cover some other link that breaks later;
#   * a row whose link has recovered is reported too — as "delete this row".
#     The registry is not allowed to quietly outlive its reason.
#   <link exactly as written in the markdown> <TAB> <expires YYYY-MM-DD> <TAB> <owner> <TAB> <what we are waiting for>
